video_caption: The video opens with a middle-aged man with grey hair, wearing a dark grey button-up sweater, speaking directly to the camera from a living room setting. Behind him, numerous running medals hang on the upper left wall, a large clock is on the upper right, a white sofa is visible on the left, and a red wall-mounted shelf displaying items and the word "ZWIFT" in white text is on the right. From 0:07 to 0:10, an animated logo appears, showing an orange film strip with three frames, each containing a black silhouette of a runner in a different pose, alongside the 3D orange text "Film My Run" on a white background with a subtle dotted pattern. The man returns to speaking, and at 0:16, a celebratory image overlays the screen, featuring two smiling men—Kilian Jornet (left, dark hair, dark jacket over a red hoodie, holding a blue cup) and Zach Miller (right, lighter hair, white cap, and a white t-shirt with "WALLS ARE MEANT FOR CLIMBING" in black text)—against a sparkling, confetti-like background with the overlaid text "Happy New Year from Kilian and Zach!". The man then resumes speaking until 0:25, when a screenshot of a Strava activity post by "Jim Walmsley" titled "So what do we race next year then?" dated October 27, 2023, is displayed. The post details a 15.44 km run with 1,194 m elevation gain over 2h 16m, featuring a map of a mountainous route, two scenic photos, and Jim Walmsley's overall Strava statistics, including a detailed list of HOKA running shoes and their logged distances. The man reappears at 0:38 and continues to speak.

The video segment opens with an animated scene featuring Peter Griffin from Family Guy, bald and wearing a white shirt and green pants, holding a newspaper and smoking, looking surprised as he speaks to Brian, a white dog with a red collar, who is sitting next to a small record player on a table. This transitions to a live-action shot of a middle-aged man with short grey hair and a dark grey button-up sweater, sitting on a white couch, speaking directly to the camera; behind him, multiple medals hang on the wall, and a white shelf holds red bottles. The scene then shifts to a white background displaying four sets of text and logos, each representing a race category: "UTMB®", "CCC®", "TDS®", and "OCC". Each category lists "Points nécessaires" (Necessary points) and "Points actuels" (Current points), with "KO" (knock-out) or "OK" indicators in red or green circles, illustrating a point system. The video returns to the man speaking on the couch, followed by a meme image of Dory from Finding Nemo with the text "I'M NEVER RUNNING AGAIN" above her and "OH LOOK! A RACE!" below, humorously depicting a runner's changing mindset. The man on the couch reappears, and then an animated cartoon illustration shows a bustling race start line with a large arch labeled "UTMB POINTS" and "START," surrounded by various sponsor logos. A grinning "RUNNING DIRECTOR" in a cap and vest stands prominently, holding a stopwatch and a large wad of cash, with money falling around him, while numerous male runners are positioned at the start. The man on the couch speaks again before the video cuts to another animated illustration of a race finish line marked "THE END." Here, a man with a dog's face in a trench coat and a flowered hat stands with crossed arms, looking unamused, while a man with orange hair and a colorful shirt, and two other men (one bearded in a blue shirt, another in a flamboyant feathery costume) run towards the finish line. The segment concludes with the man on the couch speaking one last time.

The video opens with a middle-aged man with short grey hair, wearing a dark grey knitted sweater, sitting on a light-colored sofa and speaking directly to the camera. Behind him, a wall is adorned with numerous running medals, and to his right, a white shelf holds various bottles and an orange fabric item marked "ZWIFT", with a large clock above. The scene then transitions to a white screen displaying "MY 2022 QUALIFYING POINTS" and four sections detailing entry conditions and points for races like "UTMB®", "CCC®", "TDS®", and "OCC®", including "Running Stones" (e.g., 100K M 709). A red rectangular highlight appears around the "Entry conditions" and "Current points" for UTMB, which states: "Entry conditions : 10 Points with 2 races or at least 1 Stone & a valid Index Current points : 8 Points". The man reappears, animatedly speaking, before the screen transitions to a title card with a scenic mountainous background, featuring a red-bearded runner on the right and large white text reading "UTMB WENT TOO FAR THIS TIME" with an orange banner below stating "GARY ROBBINS IS FUMING". Following this, two overlapping news article screenshots are displayed; the top one is titled "New Ultra Trail Whistler by UTMB Exposes Sport's Growing Pains" and the one below it is titled "Local Race Org., UTMB World Series, and Whistler Blackcomb Clash Over New Race Announcement". The man reappears, speaking and pointing his right index finger upwards, after which an animated logo "Film My Run" (showing running silhouettes within a film strip) is displayed. The man returns, speaking with expressive gestures, leading to an animated cartoon illustration of a large, startled-looking man with a red beard and a blue cap (featuring a Canadian maple leaf) running frantically on railroad tracks while holding a "UTMB" flag, being pursued by a crowd of angry, smaller men, some in a mine cart, with a mountain and forest backdrop. The video concludes with the man speaking to the camera with varied facial expressions, from serious to slightly exasperated.

The video opens with a man, likely in his 50s or 60s, with short grey hair and a fair complexion, speaking directly to the camera. He wears a dark grey, long-sleeved, quarter-button sweater. Behind him, a cream-colored couch, a wall clock with Roman numerals, a collection of medals, and a red banner with "ZWIFT" in white text are visible. The scene transitions to a screenshot of a webpage titled "OPEN LETTER TO THE TRAIL RUNNING COMMUNITY" (English: "OPEN LETTER TO THE TRAIL RUNNING COMMUNITY"), set against a scenic backdrop of a mountain lake. The letter's body text discusses UTMB World Series' engagement with Coast Mountain Trail Running (CMTR) in North America and addresses mischaracterizations of their intentions. The video briefly returns to the man speaking before transitioning to a title card. This card prominently displays "THE IRONMAN GROUP" (English: "THE IRONMAN GROUP") logo, featuring a red circle with a black 'i', along with the text "THEIR SIDE OF THE WHISTLER STORY" (English: "THEIR SIDE OF THE WHISTLER STORY"). This text is superimposed over a blurred image of a male runner wearing a dark blue long-sleeved top and a running vest, suggesting a trail running context.

The video opens with a still image of a man and a woman, both wearing light blue Hawaiian-style shirts, posing at what appears to be a running race finish line. The man on the right, smiling broadly, holds a microphone aloft, while the woman on the left leans her head against his shoulder with a gentle smile. Behind them, a large digital clock displays "15:04:02," and many people, some in blue shirts, are visible in the background on a red running track. The scene then transitions to an Instagram post featuring the same image, with text from "corrinemalcolm" reading: "Well team, I’ve got some bad news for you. There is one place I won’t be in 2024 - and that’s behind the mic for UTMB Live. As of yesterday I’ve been informed that I can no longer be part of the commentary team that I’ve worked with for the last four years because I’m too outspoken. And they’re not wrong, you’ll always know where I stand. There’s been alot of *us vs them* or" (This text is already in English). The video then cuts to a man with short grey hair, wearing a dark grey button-up sweater, speaking to the camera from an indoor setting with numerous medals hanging on the wall behind him. This shot briefly transitions to a news article headline overlaid on the initial image, stating: "UTMB fires livestream commentator Corrine Malcolm" (This text is already in English), with a sub-headline "The ultra-trail community is lamenting what it views as the latest misstep by UTMB/Ironman" (This text is already in English). Following this, a podcast episode screen appears, titled "Ep 524 - UTMB Commentator Fired For Being Too Outspoken - Corrine Malcolm" (This text is already in English), with "Bad Boy Running" as the podcast name. The video concludes with the man in the grey sweater speaking to the camera again, offering a slight smile.

The video segment opens with a screenshot of "The Green Runners" website, displaying a green circular logo, a navigation bar with options like "HOME" and "JOIN US," and a collage of people in outdoor settings holding signs. To the right, a "WELCOME TO The Green Runners" message describes it as "A running community making changes for a fitter planet," with a "JOIN US NOW!" button. The scene transitions to a middle-aged man with grey hair, wearing a dark buttoned-up sweater, sitting on a light-colored couch and speaking directly to the camera; behind him are hanging medals and a shelf with bottles. This is followed by a triumphant male runner in a red t-shirt and headband, arms raised and shouting, celebrating in an outdoor setting with buildings and flags in the background. The man on the couch returns briefly before the video shows a split screen: a mountain landscape with trail runners on the left, and an orange Dacia Duster SUV with a man opening its door on the right, labeled with "UTMB WORLD SERIES" and "DACIA" logos and the text "OFFICIAL AUTOMOTIVE PARTNER." The man on the couch reappears for a moment, and the segment concludes with a wide shot of a running race starting line packed with participants under a large archway. The archway prominently displays "UTMB WORLD SERIES," "DACIA UTMB MONT-BLANC," "CHAMONIX MONT-BLANC," and other sponsor logos like Hoka and Wahoo, with a digital clock showing "0:05:03" above the crowd, and a red circle highlights the "DACIA UTMB MONT-BLANC" logo.

The video segment opens at 0:07 with a screenshot of a "Runner's World" article titled "Kilian Jornet withdraws from UTMB due to injury." A section of the article, "As a four-time winner and course record holder, the Spanish athlete has withdrawn from the biggest trail ultramarathon in the world due to a sacrum injury," is highlighted in purple. An advertisement for "Weather ready - anytime, anywhere" with a runner is visible on the right. At 0:10, the screen changes to a "trailrunner" article with a similar headline and a black-and-white image of Kilian Jornet. From 0:15 to 0:19, a man with short grey hair and a black button-up sweater sits on a light-colored couch, speaking directly to the camera. Medals hang on the wall to his left, and a white shelf with orange items and a clock are on his right. At 0:19, the video transitions to a crowded race start line for the "UTMB World Series," featuring a large blue and black archway with sponsor logos such as "DACIA UTMB MONT-BLANC," "HOKA FLY HUMAN FLY," and "WAHOO." A large clock on the arch shows "17:59:03." A red circle highlights the "DACIA UTMB MONT-BLANC" logo. This scene zooms in slightly at 0:22, with the clock now showing "18:00:09," and a red line points to the "WAHOO" logo while a red circle still highlights the "UTMB MONT-BLANC" text. The man in the black sweater reappears from 0:27 to 0:29. From 0:29 to 0:31, a different man wearing a white cap, red running vest, and water bottles is seen inside what appears to be a race tent, looking at the camera. Behind him, a "DACIA" banner is visible and highlighted with a red circle. The man in the black sweater reappears briefly at 0:32. The segment concludes at 0:34 with an image of three male runners in athletic wear, arms raised in triumph, standing on a blue track at a finish line, with numerous spectators and sponsor logos like "DACIA," "WAHOO," and "HOKA FLY HUMAN FLY" in the background.

The video segment opens with a middle-aged man, sporting short grey hair and a stubble beard, speaking directly to the camera from a light-colored sofa. He wears a dark grey fleece jacket, and the background reveals a wall adorned with numerous hanging medals and a white shelf holding red bottles or containers, with a large white clock to the right. A "WORLD TRAIL MAJORS" logo, featuring stylized black "W" and "M" with a green "T" resembling mountains, is overlaid on the bottom left. The scene then transitions to a full-screen graphic displaying the "WORLD TRAIL MAJORS 2024 SCHEDULE," a green table listing 8 trail running events across the globe, including their dates, distances, elevation gains, and locations, each with its respective logo. Following an animated "Film My Run" logo depicting a film strip with three running silhouettes, the man reappears, introducing an email from Kilian Jornet and Zach Miller. The email text, shown as a white overlay on a dark background, invites top athletes to consider racing each other at events other than UTMB in 2024, acknowledging their existing ties to UTMB. Finally, the man returns on screen, encouraging viewers to engage with the video as a YouTube overlay with "thumbs up" and "thumbs down" icons, a "SUBSCRIBE" button (which animates to show a bell icon with notification waves when clicked), and a bell icon appears at the bottom of the screen.

The video segment opens with a close-up of text on a screen, which reads: "our efforts can be a bit more focused and not so overwhelming. Having said that, what is this all about? Well, we are writing to you to see if you might be interested in committing to racing each other at a race other than UTMB this year (2024). While we realize that many of you may have strong ties to UTMB (personal goals, incentives from sponsors, career goals, etc.) we ask that you hear us out on what we have to say here." (This text is an invitation for athletes to consider participating in a race other than UTMB in 2024, acknowledging the strong ties many have to UTMB.) The scene then cuts to a man with short, grey hair, wearing a dark grey or black knitted sweater with a zip-up collar, sitting on a white sofa. He is looking slightly down and to his right, speaking. In the background, there's a light-colored wall adorned with a collection of medals on the left and a white wall clock on the right, with a small orange shelf holding several bottles beneath it. The video then transitions back to a close-up of text, which states: "First off, we want to acknowledge that UTMB is a great race, even though there has been a lot of drama recently, we still feel that the race and the organization have done a lot of good for the sport of ultra running. Thanks to UTMB, we now have a world championship-esque event that draws many of the best runners in the sport as well as sponsors, media, and fans from all over the world. It has truly become the big event of the year and has really helped to put our sport on the map. Having an event like this has created a lot of opportunity for people like ourselves, as it drives a lot of money and attention to the sport. This, we feel, is a good thing." (This text acknowledges UTMB's positive contributions to ultra-running, despite recent issues, highlighting its role as a major event that has elevated the sport globally.) The phrase "It has truly become the big event of the year and has really helped to put our sport on the map." is highlighted in blue.

The video opens with a digital screen displaying text on a light beige background, detailing concerns about UTMB, UTMB Group, and Ironman's management practices, stating, "However, while it may be good for the sport to grow and develop in these ways, it is also important that the growth occurs in a positive, healthy manner. Unfortunately, the current direction that UTMB, UTMB Group, and Ironman have taken has given us cause for concern. There are a multitude of things that we could point to that are concerning to us, but the gist of it is that we feel that they are not managing themselves and their event(s) in a way that has the best interest of the sport and its people in mind." A blue highlight then emphasizes the phrase "we feel that they are not managing themselves and their event(s) in a way that has the best interest of the sport and its people in mind." The scene transitions to a man with short grey hair and a black collared sweater, sitting on a light-colored couch, speaking directly to the camera with a serious expression. Medals hang on the wall behind him to the left, and a white shelf with red and white items and bottles is to his right, with a clock above it. The video then returns to the text screen, which continues, "we are alright with the organization making money. However, we feel that there is a way to do this without treating people poorly and running over everyone who gets in your way. To put it simply, we want them to run their business well. We want them to be considerate. We want them to not only ask "what can we do to benefit ourselves?", but also "what can we do to improve the sport of trail running as a whole?". Unfortunately, we feel that they have not been doing a very good job with this. And while it would be nice to be able to sit down and chat with them so that we can course correct and get things back on track, we fear". A blue highlight appears, emphasizing "We want them to not only ask "what can we do to benefit ourselves?", but also "what can we do to improve the sport of trail running as a whole?"." The man reappears on screen, speaking to the camera with a slightly more neutral and calm expression, concluding the segment.

The video segment opens with black text on a light-beige background, proposing a strategy to communicate discontent and apply pressure: "Perhaps the best way to communicate our discontent and apply some pressure is to band together and all go to a different race. An absence of the top fifteen ranked male and female runners from the UTMB start line would speak volumes. It would communicate to them that we are not happy and pressure them to make some changes. So, we would like to hear your thoughts. We have already pin-pointed a potential race that we could attend instead of UTMB, but before we get into all that, please let us know what you think. Do you have the same or similar concerns? Are you interested in". The phrases "An absence of the top fifteen ranked male and female runners from the UTMB start line would speak volumes." and "We have already pin-pointed a potential race that we could attend instead of UTMB" are highlighted in light blue. This transitions to a middle-aged man with short grey hair, wearing a dark grey collared shirt, sitting on a light-colored sofa. Behind him, a wall is adorned with numerous medals on the left, and a white shelf holding orange bottles and a red item labeled "ZWIFT" on the right. He speaks earnestly, and then the screen displays a "WORLD TRAIL MAJORS 2024 SCHEDULE" table on a green background. The table lists several races with their dates, distances, elevations, and locations. A red curved line highlights two specific races: "Quebec - Canada" (160 km, +6500 m) and "Cape Town - South Africa" (166 km, +7516 m). The man reappears briefly, continuing to speak, before the text screen returns. The new text states: "Please let us know so that we can continue the dialogue and discuss what the next steps might be. And please realize, this is not meant to be a malicious, hateful thing towards UTMB. The idea here is to find a way to apply some pressure to the UTMB/Ironman organization so that we can effect positive change. It would be great if one day we could go to UTMB and feel good about it, knowing that what they are doing is making the sport better, not worse." The sentence "The idea here is to find a way to apply some pressure to the UTMB/Ironman organization so that we can effect positive change." is highlighted in light blue. The video concludes with a logo animation featuring an orange filmstrip with three frames, each containing a black silhouette of a runner in motion, appearing on a white background. Below the filmstrip, the words "Film My Run" animate in, with "Film" in orange and "My Run" in grey, in a digital-style font.

In this video segment, a middle-aged man with short grey hair, wearing a dark grey knitted sweater, speaks directly to the camera while seated on a light-colored sofa. Behind him, a wall is adorned with numerous medals, and to his right, a white shelf holds bottles next to a red item with "ZWIFT" printed on it, all beneath a round clock. From 0:14, a yellow emoji appears on his left cheek, and an Instagram-like overlay slides in from the right, partially obscuring the background. On-screen text reads "WHICH MEANS FOR ME," followed by "ALL THREE ARE" (incomplete). The Instagram feed displays comments: "filmyrun" (username visible), "running_squirrel Ekkkk! I'm in shock!" (username and comment visible), and "tomevansultra Got it in one" (username and comment visible), which is highlighted by a white circle, along with other partially visible comments below. The Instagram overlay disappears at 0:21, and the man continues speaking with a more serious expression. From 0:26, several brand logos appear around him: "adidas" (top left), "HOKA FLY HUMAN FLY" (bottom left), "INOV8" (top right), and "Salomon S" (bottom right), as he concludes his statement with a slight smirk and a gesture as if blowing a kiss.

The video opens with a middle-aged man with short grey hair and a dark grey button-up top speaking directly to the camera, with a wide-mouthed, animated expression. He is seated on a light-colored sofa in a room with a white wall, where a collection of medals hangs in the background on the left, and a white shelf with various items and a red "ZWIFT" branded cloth are visible on the right, along with a large wall clock. Superimposed around the man are the black logos for "adidas" and "inov-8", the blue logo for "HOKA FLY HUMAN FLY," and the black logo for "Salomon S." As he continues to speak, his expression becomes more serious, and the logos disappear. The scene then transitions to a black screen displaying an Instagram post from "vo2maxcoaching" located in "Chamonix, France." The post reads: "What really baffles me about the campaign of hate that's currently being waged against UTMB is that, more than any any [sic] other race, UTMB has allowed Jornet and many of his fellow pros to climb aboard the mountain-ultra-trail money-train and become financially secure and moderately influential. So it seems to be a little ungrateful to then turn around and attempt to hold the race to ransom. This year half of the athletes I coach will be racing at UTMB in one of the races. This makes me very proud of all of them. I am proud because they have all worked their butts off and made some difficult lifestyle choices over the last few years to make it into this race. I am proud because the UTMB races are" (the text is cut off at the end). The video then cuts back to the man, who now has a more thoughtful and less animated expression as he continues his discussion.

A man with grey hair and a fair complexion, wearing a dark grey or black long-sleeved buttoned shirt, is seated on a light-colored couch, looking directly at the camera and speaking animatedly. He occasionally blinks and subtly moves his head while talking. In the background to his left, a wall is covered with numerous running medals hanging on ribbons, illuminated by a warm light from below. To his right, a white shelf holds several small red objects, possibly sports-related items, and beneath it hangs a red fabric with white text that appears to read "ZWIFT." A large white wall clock with black roman numerals is visible above the shelf. The scene remains static throughout the segment.

The video opens with a man with graying hair wearing a dark gray ribbed sweater, speaking directly to the camera while seated on a light-colored sofa, gesturing occasionally with his hands. Behind him, a wall is adorned with numerous running medals and a large white clock with Roman numerals, while to his right, a white shelf unit holds small red and clear bottles, with an orange item below it labeled "ZWIFT". At 0:21, the scene briefly transitions to a game show set from "WOULD I LIE TO YOU?", showing a man with brown hair gesturing with his right hand near his face and speaking, alongside a woman with pink hair and a headscarf looking at him with a serious expression. The video then cuts back to the first man, who continues speaking, sometimes smiling, and at 0:27, points his right index finger to the right side of the frame, maintaining eye contact with the camera.
